# Fixtures of the contextualizer

The unit tests of `src/context/` and `src/provider/contextualize/` read nothing outside
this crate's tree except the migration (see below), so a test that cannot find its
contract fails instead of passing by not running. Nothing here is typed by hand to make a
test pass: each file is either generated by the code that owns the contract, or is a
golden of this crate's own output that a person reviews as a diff.

## `contracts/`

| File | Owner and generator | What the tests do with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `infer-statuses.json` | inference-core: `MP_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p inference-core --lib status_contract` in `apps/Model Plane/rust` | `context/outcome/tests.rs` decodes every case with the real decoder and compares the outcome with the table of decisions; the table fails when the contract gains a case nobody decided about. `provider/contextualize/tests.rs` builds the refusals and throttles it sends from the same cases. |
| `inference-service-tokens.golden.json` | Auth Core: `UPDATE_CONTRACT_GOLDEN=1 npx jest inference-service-token.contract` in `apps/Control Plane/auth-core` | `provider/contextualize/tests.rs` serves each captured answer (real compact JWTs, the real 503 and 403 bodies) to the REAL token client, which applies all of its claim checks. A loopback server is only the transport. |
| `infer-response-azure-live.json` | The live proof: `provider::contextualize::live_proof` (below) | `context/validate/tests.rs` holds the validation to what Azure OpenAI really answers. |

Both vendored files are byte-for-byte copies with a sha256 pin beside them (the sha256 of
the file with CRLF normalised to LF). `context/testing.rs` checks the pin on every read
and panics on a missing or altered file. The repo-level check
`scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh` fails when a copy differs from its original.
Never edit a copy: regenerate it from its owner, copy the file and its pin here.

### `infer-response-azure-live.json`: not captured yet

Until the live proof has run, this file does not exist. The validation test that reads it
prints `pending` and passes, and FAILS when `REQUIRE_CONTRACT` is set: the task is not
proven until the real answer has been recorded, and a build that says it is complete must
not pass without it.

It matters for one reason in particular. An earlier design required the finish reason
`end_turn`. inference-core returns the provider's own finish reason, which for Azure
OpenAI is `stop`, so that rule would have rejected every real answer, and a hand-written
test would never have shown it. The unit tests of `validate.rs` therefore use the
finish reasons inference-core's adapters emit (read from `openai.rs`), and this file is
the record of what a real deployment sent.

Capture it (four paid calls, about 0.002 USD, against a throwaway organization; the
runbook has the full procedure and the pass criteria):

    CR_LIVE_ORG_ID=<throwaway organization id> CR_LIVE_WRITE_CAPTURE=1 \
      bash tests/scripts/contextual-retrieval-live-proof.sh

The document it sends is synthetic (an invented company), so the contexts it records are
not a customer's content. The file holds four cases (three chunks with finish reason
`stop`, one with `length` from a 16-token cap) with the fields of the response the
contextualizer reads: `stop_reason`, `model_used`, `provider_used`, `residency`, the
token counts including `cache_read_input_tokens`, `usage_reported`, `response_cache_hit`
and the text.

## `prompts/`

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx-v1.en.golden.txt`, `ctx-v1.nb.golden.txt` | The prompt every stored context was generated from. Produced by compiling and running the `build_prompt` function of `provider/contextualize.rs` as it was at git HEAD before this task, on the two inputs the test uses. NEVER regenerated: the test that reads them is what keeps the default prompt byte-identical to what shipped. |
| `ctx-v2.nb.golden.txt` | The `ctx-v2` prompt for a Norwegian chunk, written by this crate's code. Regenerate on purpose with `UPDATE_PROMPT_GOLDENS=1 cargo test -p embedding-engine-rs ctx_v2_matches_its_golden`, review the diff, and bump the prompt version in the same change: a different prompt is a different version. |

## The migration

`context/outcome/tests.rs` compares `Status` and `ErrorClass` with the CHECK constraints
of `infra/postgres/migrations/20261003130000_context_provenance.sql`. The Docker build
context holds `services/` only and runs no tests, so the comparison is skipped when the
file is not there; a checkout that is complete (`REQUIRE_CONTRACT` or `CI`) fails instead.
